title: K-ABENA: K-Adaptive Backpropagation with Error-based N-exclusion Algorithm : (Compensated Loss-Based Sample Exclusion with Unbiased Gradient Estimation)
summary: The paper addresses the bias of loss-based selective backpropagation, where skipping low-loss samples saves backward passes but gives a loss-correlated, biased gradient. K-ABENA v3 uses a defensive-mixture sampling design over the minor set with Horvitz-Thompson/Hajek inverse-probability reweighting, plus theory for design-unbiasedness, self-normalization bias, and SGD convergence. On real scikit-learn datasets v3 matches full-batch SGD, e.g. Breast Cancer logistic regression 0.9706 while saving 28.5%, and on a 0.17%-imbalance fraud replica it reaches AUC 0.9991 versus 0.9998 for full batch.

match_target.why: C1 is the direct user hint and the cheapest claim that still shows the paper's central parity result: v3 matches full-batch SGD on the smallest real benchmark, Table 1's Breast Cancer logistic regression; C2 records the same row's 28.5% saving.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: bounded accuracy on the 143-example Breast Cancer test set (below 2,000), and the paper prints accuracies as fractions in [0,1], so 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Run the benchmark with full-batch SGD, recalibrating K each epoch at the 40th percentile of current losses, with default N=0.3 and α=0.3.

requirements.stmt: Partition samples by loss threshold K into the minor set with li≤K and its complement; always retain all major samples.
requirements.quote: partitions the indices into the minor set M = {i : li ≤K}, k = |M|, and the major set Mc

requirements.stmt: Set the number of retained minors to m = round(N k), as in the paper's finite retention budget.
requirements.quote: A retention proportion N ∈(0, 1) fixes the number of retained minors m = ⌊Nk⌉.

requirements.stmt: Sample exactly m minors without replacement using the defensive-mixture single-draw probabilities in Eq. 1.
requirements.quote: Draw S ⊂M, |S| = m, without replacement with single-draw probabilities

requirements.stmt: For α<1, use inclusion probabilities πi = m pi under the stated Poisson/rejective approximation; for α=1 use exact πi=m/k.
requirements.quote: we use the Poisson/rejective approximation πi = m pi, standard for high-entropy without-replacement designs

requirements.stmt: Implement the Horvitz-Thompson form with majors weighted by 1 and selected minors weighted by 1/πi for the design-unbiased estimator.
